subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Bias-Variance Tradeoff in Human Judgment
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Bias-Variance Tradeoff in Human Judgment.

hook.text: A weather model that perfectly predicts last year's weather often fails tomorrow. It memorized, not learned.

buildup.text: In machine learning, the bias-variance tradeoff shows that flexibility creates accuracy on old data but errors on new.

discovery.text: Human heuristics are biased but low-variance. They give consistent answers that perform well on average.

twist.text: A complex thinker who tries to weight everything may overfit to today's situation and fail tomorrow.

climax.text: Some bias is the cost of being robust. A slightly wrong but consistent rule beats a precise but fragile one.

punchline.text: A little bias buys a lot of stability.

quiz.question: What is the tradeoff in human heuristics?
options: Some bias in exchange for consistent, robust performance
